headline: BDT 4,469 crore financial irregularities found in Shahjalal Airport Third Terminal project audit
summary: A government audit revealed massive financial misconduct in the BDT 21,300 crore project, including unauthorized payments and contract violations across 27 sectors. The current government is reviewing the findings.
details: A government audit has uncovered financial irregularities totaling BDT 4,469 crore (approximately USD 400 million) in the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport's Third Terminal project. This massive financial loss was identified across various sectors by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) office.

The BDT 21,300 crore project, one of Bangladesh's largest infrastructure initiatives, saw hundreds of crores paid outside contractual agreements, additional bills approved without authorization, and failure to collect compensation from contractors for delayed work. The project began on December 28, 2019, under the previous government.

The CAG report details 27 categories of irregularities, including consultants approving variations without proper authority, leading to irregular expenses of BDT 1,989 crore. International contract norms were not followed, and approval limits were exceeded.

Further findings include BDT 122 crore paid to contractors for inflated weights beyond proposed amounts, and BDT 70 crore for "value engineering" by showing fictitious savings despite increased contract value.

Significant irregularities were also found in soil removal, where contractors billed for transporting soil 6.5 kilometers away but disposed of it within two kilometers, causing a BDT 52 crore loss. Payments were also made without necessary administrative approvals.

The audit highlighted weaknesses in project authority oversight, including inadequate verification of contractor claims and failure to enforce contract terms. Concerns were raised about a lack of effective checks and balances, as the development partner, consultant, and contractor were all from the same country.

Additional financial losses include BDT 71 lakh for extra airfare for consultants, BDT 11 crore for double payments for consultant car rentals, and BDT 39 crore for fees to consultants not listed in the contract.

The project also saw goods imported from unauthorized countries like China and India, instead of those specified in the contract (Italy, Singapore, Thailand, Korea). A BDT 44 crore payment for a "soft opening" was also made without any provision in the Development Project Proposal (DPP) or contract.

headline_marked: [[Md. Shahabuddin to leave Bangabhaban today]] after early resignation due to health reasons
headline: Md. Shahabuddin to leave Bangabhaban today after early resignation due to health reasons
summary: Former President Md. Shahabuddin will move to his Gulshan residence. Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed has assumed duties as acting President and will operate from Bangabhaban.
details: Former President Md. Shahabuddin is set to leave Bangabhaban today, Sunday (July 26), and move to his private residence in Gulshan, Dhaka. He had already held farewell meetings with officials and staff.

Md. Shahabuddin resigned from the presidency nearly two years before his term was due to end, citing health reasons. In accordance with the constitution, Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed has taken over as the acting President due to the vacancy.

Following his resignation, questions arose about where the former President would reside. It has been confirmed that Md. Shahabuddin will move into his own flat in Gulshan, where necessary preparations have been completed and security has been enhanced.

Meanwhile, acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed continues to reside in the Speaker's official residence. Security measures there have also been strengthened, with control taken by PGR-SSF. Although he will stay at his residence, he will conduct all official activities from Bangabhaban.
